title: Phase 2 IR pass prototype: validate no-LLVM-fork architecture
description: Validate the claim in docs/llvm-fork-analysis.md that CQ_lang can be built without forking LLVM. Build a minimal pass plugin against stock LLVM 19 that performs forward taint propagation and lowers a hand-written Stage 4 IR snippet (two cq_init_i32 calls, one tainted add, one cq_measure) to cqrt_* runtime calls. The pass must run on stock opt/clang and produce well-formed IR. Project-trajectory-defining sanity check — locks in the entire compiler architecture if it succeeds, surfaces fork pressure if it does not.
design: Strictly minimal scope: i32 only (no other widths), no uncomputation (Phase 5 deferred), no region handling (cq_when_*), no specialization synthesis, no function-signature rewriting beyond linear case. New PassManager (LLVM 13+) pass-plugin shape. Hand-written Stage 4 IR as input (rewriter integration deferred). cqrt_template_add_i32 declared as extern (body deferred to template library work). cqrt_* runtime stubs sufficient — no real gate emission for this validation.
acceptance_criteria: 1. libcq_pass.so builds against stock LLVM 19 (no LLVM source patches). 2. opt -load-pass-plugin ./libcq_pass.so -passes=cq-lowering test/input.ll runs without crash. 3. Output IR passes opt -verify. 4. Output IR contains: cqrt_alloc_classical_i32 calls replacing @cq_init_i32; cqrt_template_add_i32 call replacing tainted add i32; cqrt_measure replacing @cq_measure. 5. Pass plugin C++ source < 500 LOC. 6. README.md documents build/run/scope.
notes: Companion docs: docs/llvm-fork-analysis.md (the claim being validated), docs/architecture.md §3.5 / §7 (pipeline spec), docs/backend.md §3-§5 (IR pass spec). Build env per build-env-cmake-3-31-6-clang-19 memory: cmake 3.31.6, clang-19, llvm-19-dev at /usr/lib/llvm-19. Estimated 2-3 days focused implementation. Follow-up issues to file on completion: Phase 5 uncomputation prototype increment; real cqrt_template_add_i32 implementation; rewriter→prototype integration.
close_reason: Prototype validates the no-LLVM-fork architecture claim. cq_pass.cpp (254 LOC) builds against stock LLVM 19.1.7, runs via opt-19 -load-pass-plugin without crash, produces well-formed IR (passes opt -verify), and substitutes all expected lowerings (cq_init_i32→cqrt_alloc_classical_i32, tainted add→cqrt_template_add_i32, cq_measure→cqrt_measure). All 10 smoke-test checks pass. See bd memory prototype-validated-no-fork-2026-05-22.

title: Phase 4 prototype: validate region handling (cq_when_*) on stock LLVM
description: Add a fourth pass cq-control that, within cq_when_begin/cq_when_end brackets, substitutes each cqrt_template_* call with its _controlled variant (taking the region's control handle as an additional first argument). Validates that region detection + controlled-variant substitution is implementable on stock LLVM, which is the one architectural mechanism (region handling) the existing Phase 2/5/7 prototypes have not touched.
design: cq-control operates on post-lowering IR (after cq-lowering has dissolved qint_mid_t and emitted cqrt_*). For prototype simplicity, the test input declares cq_when_begin as taking i32 directly (the handle), avoiding the qint_mid_t→handle resolution that real integration would need. Linear CFG only — begin and end in same BB. No nested regions. The mechanism: walk each BB, track 'current control' state, for each cqrt_template_* call inside a region emit a _controlled variant with the control prepended to args, erase brackets at end.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Pass plugin builds against stock LLVM 19 (additions only — existing passes unaffected). 2. opt-19 -load-pass-plugin -passes=cq-control runs without crash on hand-written post-lowering input. 3. Output passes opt -verify. 4. cq_when_begin and cq_when_end call sites erased. 5. cqrt_template_add_i32 inside the region is replaced by cqrt_template_add_i32_controlled with the control handle as the first argument. 6. cqrt_template_* calls OUTSIDE any region are NOT substituted (verified by adding a second template call after cq_when_end).
notes: Out of scope for this validation increment: qint_mid_t→handle resolution at cq_when_begin (would be an extension to cq-lowering); cross-BB regions (real cq_when_* can span branches); nested regions (multi-control accumulation); the inverse case cq_invert_begin/_end (separate but similar mechanism reusing emit_inverse from Phase 5). Companion: docs/architecture.md §5.1 + §7.5 (region brackets), docs/backend.md §5.9 (region handling spec).

title: Phase 5 multi-BB validation increment
description: Extend Phase 5 prototype with a test input that exercises non-trivial CFG (branched control flow, one handle used in both arms of an if). Verifies PostDominatorTree.findNearestCommonDominator correctly identifies the merge block as the post-dominator of all uses, and that cqrt_free is inserted at the merge point (not duplicated into either branch arm). Retires the only architectural-validation residual the original Phase 5 prototype did not exercise (it ran on linear single-BB IR).
design: Hand-crafted Stage 4 IR with one cq_init_i32 in entry block, branch to then/else arms that each measure the value, merge block with phi + ret. The handle's post-dominator is the merge block; algorithm should insert there. No code changes to cq_pass.cpp expected — this validates that the existing computeFreePoint() handles the multi-BB case correctly, which is the architecturally-novel question.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Pass plugin builds (no code changes needed — same cq-uncompute pass). 2. opt-19 -load-pass-plugin -passes='cq-lowering,cq-uncompute' on multi-BB input runs without crash. 3. Output passes opt -verify. 4. cqrt_free is emitted in the merge basic block (post-dominator of both arms). 5. cqrt_free is NOT emitted in either branch arm. 6. Output has exactly one cqrt_free per handle (no duplication).
notes: Companion: prototype/test/input.ll (linear case), prototype/test/run_test_phase5.sh (existing test). New: prototype/test/input_phase5_branch.ll + prototype/test/run_test_phase5_branch.sh. If the existing pass doesn't handle multi-BB correctly, that's a fix to make — but the design (findNearestCommonDominator + getFirstInsertionPt fallback) should already be correct.
close_reason: Phase 5 multi-BB validation succeeds. Hand-crafted Stage 4 IR with branch (entry → then/else → merge), one cq_init_i32 in entry, measure in both arms. opt-19 -passes='cq-lowering,cq-uncompute' produces exactly one cqrt_free emitted in the merge block (post-dominator) — not duplicated into either arm. PostDominatorTree.findNearestCommonDominator(then, else) correctly returns merge; getFirstInsertionPt() places the free at the right point (between phi and ret). No code changes were needed — existing computeFreePoint() handles multi-BB correctly. See prototype/test/input_phase5_branch.ll, run_test_phase5_branch.sh.

title: Phase 7 prototype: validate call-graph specialization on stock LLVM
description: Extend the prototype/ pass plugin with a third pass cq-specialize that demonstrates function cloning + call-site retargeting via stock LLVM CloneFunction / CloneFunctionInto + ValueToValueMapTy. For each call site with a qint_mid_t-typed argument, clone the callee, rename to __cq_q_<f>_q1, and retarget the call site. Validates that the Phase 7 mechanism (call-graph specialization synthesis) is implementable on stock LLVM with no fork.
design: Use CloneFunction(F, VMap) to clone the callee preserving signature. Set linkage to private/internal so DCE can remove the original if all uses are retargeted. Rename via Function::setName. Walk call sites of the original; for each whose arg is qint_mid_t-typed, replace setCalledFunction to the clone. Minimal scope: signature is preserved, no Bennett wrap-around (forward + CNOT-copy + reverse) — that is downstream implementation that uses the same already-validated emit_inverse mechanism from Phase 5. The point here is to confirm CloneFunction + call-site retargeting compose with the existing cq-lowering pass.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Pass plugin builds against stock LLVM 19 (no patches). 2. opt-19 -load-pass-plugin -passes=cq-specialize runs without crash on a test input with one function-call site. 3. Output IR passes opt -verify. 4. A new function named __cq_q_<original>_q1 exists in the module. 5. The clone has the same signature as the original (signature rewriting deferred). 6. The original call site is replaced with a call to the clone. 7. Both functions (original + clone) are well-formed.
notes: Out of scope: signature rewriting to (i32, i32) handle ABI, Bennett wrap-around (forward + CNOT-copy + reverse), specialization caching across multiple call sites, recursion handling, q-arg-mask discrimination beyond binary 'has qint_mid_t arg or not'. These are downstream once cloning + retargeting compose with lowering. Companion: bd memory prototype-validated-no-fork-2026-05-22, docs/llvm-fork-analysis.md §8.2.
close_reason: Phase 7 prototype validates call-graph specialization. cq-specialize pass uses stock LLVM CloneFunction (+ ValueToValueMapTy) to clone callees with qint_mid_t-typed args, renames via __cq_q_<f>_q1 mangling, retargets call sites. Test: opt-19 -load-pass-plugin -passes=cq-specialize produces a clone with internal linkage that preserves the original function's body shape (extractvalue + add + insertvalue + ret), call site in @example now references the clone, zero remaining calls to the original from @example, output passes opt -verify. See prototype/test/run_test_phase7.sh, prototype/test/output_phase7.ll.

title: Phase 5 prototype: validate auto-uncomputation on stock LLVM
description: Extend the prototype/ pass plugin with a second pass cq-uncompute that demonstrates last-use-driven uncomputation emission via stock LLVM PostDominatorTree analysis. For each handle SSA value (produced by cqrt_alloc_classical_i32 / cqrt_alloc_i32), compute the post-dominating last use and emit cqrt_free(handle) at that point. Skip handles that escape via ReturnInst. Validates that the Phase 5 mechanism (per-op compile-time adjoints at SSA live-range ends) is implementable on stock LLVM with no fork.
design: Use FunctionAnalysisManagerModuleProxy to obtain PostDominatorTreeAnalysis from a Module pass. Use PostDominatorTree::findNearestCommonDominator over user blocks to find the post-dominator BB; within that BB, find the latest user (linear case) and insert after. Emit cqrt_free as a placeholder for the full adjoint gate sequence — the real inverse template is downstream implementation work, not architecture validation. Single test input (same as main prototype) is sufficient: linear control flow exercises the API without needing complex CFG yet.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Pass plugin builds against stock LLVM 19 (no patches). 2. opt-19 -load-pass-plugin -passes='cq-lowering,cq-uncompute' runs without crash on input.ll. 3. Output IR passes opt -verify. 4. Each handle (cqrt_alloc_classical_i32 result, cqrt_alloc_i32 result) has a cqrt_free(handle) call emitted after its last use. 5. Handle SSA values that escape via ret are not freed. 6. Total pass plugin C++ remains focused (no bloat).
notes: Out of scope: real adjoint gate-sequence emission (cqrt_free as placeholder only), loop-aware uncomputation, multi-BB region uncomputation, multi-width. These are downstream once the core analysis-manager wiring is shown to work. Companion: bd memory prototype-validated-no-fork-2026-05-22, docs/llvm-fork-analysis.md §8.2.
close_reason: Phase 5 prototype validates auto-uncomputation. cq-uncompute pass uses stock LLVM PostDominatorTree (via FunctionAnalysisManagerModuleProxy) to compute the post-dominating last use of each handle, emits cqrt_free at that point, skips handles that escape via ret. Test pipeline: opt-19 -load-pass-plugin -passes='cq-lowering,cq-uncompute' produces 3 cqrt_free calls (one per handle), output passes opt -verify, all checks green. See prototype/test/run_test_phase5.sh, prototype/test/output_phase5.ll.

title: P11: transpiler/README.md documentation
description: Phase 11: Write transpiler/README.md documenting: prerequisites (LLVM/Clang >= 16 dev install), configure command (-DLLVM_DIR/-DClang_DIR), build target list (quantum_transpiler, quantum_transpiler_unit_tests, check-quantum), how to run a single fixture. Reference from PRD.md deliverables list.

title: P10: Full acceptance — fixture 08 + #include insertion + acceptance.sh
description: Phase 10: Add fixture 08_full_example (== example_v1). Implement #include "qint.h" insertion in Matcher (once per FileID). Run acceptance.sh: transpile example_v1.c, compile with qint.h, run binary, diff output against example_v1.expected.log. PRD criteria 2-4 must be green.

title: P9: E2E fixture 07 — multi-decl support
description: Phase 9: Add e2e fixture 07_multi_decl. May require fixes to DeclStmtRewrite range computation for multi-variable declarations (quantum int a = 3, b = 2;). 1 new fixture must pass.

title: P8: E2E fixtures 04, 05, 06 — patterns 3 and 4 (Q+Q, Q+literal, Q+classvar)
description: Phase 8: Add e2e fixtures 04_q_plus_q (pattern 3), 05_q_plus_literal and 06_q_plus_classvar (pattern 4). 3 new fixtures must pass.

title: P7: E2E fixtures 02, 03 — pattern 2 (classical init variants)
description: Phase 7: Add e2e fixtures 02_init_literal and 03_init_classvar (pattern 2 variants — literal init and classical variable init). Iterate Codegen/DeclStmtRewrite if anything bends. 2 new fixtures must pass.

title: P6: DeclStmtRewrite + Matcher + driver wired up; fixture 01 e2e
description: Phase 6: Implement DeclStmtRewrite.h/.cpp (~150 LOC) — inspects matched DeclStmt, builds VarRewriteInput, calls Codegen. Implement Matcher.h/.cpp (~120 LOC) — ASTMatchFinder wiring + Rewriter callback. Wire up main.cpp driver (~80 LOC). Unit tests (test_decl_stmt_rewrite.cpp). First e2e fixture (01_uninit) passes.

title: P5: Codegen module (pure string assembly) + tests
description: Phase 5: Implement Codegen.h/.cpp (~250 LOC). Pure string assembly — takes VarRewriteInput struct, returns rewritten string. Supports all 5 Forms: Uninit, ClassicalInit, QuantumPlusQuantum, QuantumPlusClassical, ClassicalPlusQuantum. Unit tests (test_codegen.cpp): one per Form + multi-decl + ClassicalPlusQuantum case.

title: P4: OperandClass module + tests
description: Phase 4: Implement OperandClass.h/.cpp (~120 LOC). Classifies Expr as Quantum or Classical, skipping ParenExpr/ImplicitCastExpr. Unit tests (test_operand_class.cpp): quantum var, classical var, literal, paren-wrapped quantum, implicit cast.

title: P3: QuantumAttr + SourceText modules + tests
description: Phase 3: Implement QuantumAttr.h/.cpp (~60 LOC) — hasQuantumAttr/refersToQuantumVar predicates. Implement SourceText.h/.cpp (~80 LOC) — getExprText using Lexer::getSourceText. Unit tests (test_source_text.cpp) covering both modules: quantum vs non-quantum VarDecl, DeclRefExpr walking, literal/identifier/binop/paren expression text extraction.

title: P2: TypeMap module + unit tests
description: Phase 2: Implement TypeMap.h/.cpp (~60 LOC). Maps C type (BuiltinType::Kind) to num_bits per PRD bit-width table. Unit tests (test_type_map.cpp): table-driven — Bool→1, Char→8, Short/Int→16, Long→32, LongLong→64, Float→0, Double→0.

title: P1: qint.h + example_v1.c + golden files
description: Phase 1: Hand-author qint.h (stub backend header with qint_t, init_qint, add), example_v1.c (canonical v1 input exercising all 4 patterns + multi-decl), example_v1.expected.c (golden output), and example_v1.expected.log. Sanity test: cc -include qint.h -x c /dev/null -E parses cleanly.

title: P0: Project skeleton — CMakeLists.txt finds LLVM, builds empty main.cpp that prints help
description: Phase 0: Set up transpiler/CMakeLists.txt that finds LLVM/Clang dev install, builds an empty main.cpp that prints help text. Add CTest hook (make check-quantum). Build smoke test only.
